title: Missing lemma: gradients of smooth forms should be STABLE (not just semistable) in P(W)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** Lemma `lem:ss-to-ss` (Section ef{sec:proj}); needed to close Lemma `lem:Nopen` (issue on saturation).

**Gap.** `lem:ss-to-ss` only shows $
abla(\mathbb{P}(\mathcal V)^{ss})\subseteq\mathbb{P}(\mathcal W)^{ss}$. The entire saturation difficulty in `lem:Nopen` would dissolve if in fact
$$
abla(\mathbb{P}X)\subseteq\mathbb{P}(\mathcal W)^{s}\quad(	ext{the STABLE locus}),$$
because on the stable locus the good quotient is geometric, orbits are closed, fibers are single orbits, and every $G$-invariant open is automatically saturated *within* the stable locus. The proof never addresses stability (as opposed to mere semistability) of $
abla f$.

**Suggested proof.** Use the $\mathrm{GL}_n$-equivariant left inverse $R$ from Lemma `lem:euler` ($R\circ
abla=\mathrm{id}$). For a 1-parameter subgroup $\lambda$, equivariant linear maps cannot increase the minimal Hilbert--Mumford weight; thus $\mu(
abla f,\lambda)\le 0$ would force, via $R$, $\mu(f,\lambda)=\mu(R(
abla f),\lambda)\le \mu(
abla f,\lambda)\le 0$, contradicting stability of $f$ (Lemma `lem:stable`). Hence $\mu(
abla f,\lambda)>0$ for all nontrivial $\lambda$, i.e. $
abla f$ is stable. Finite stabilizers transfer along the injective equivariant $
abla$. One must write the weight-monotonicity inequality $\mu(R(w),\lambda)\le\mu(w,\lambda)$ carefully (sign conventions) and verify proper stability.
